reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch treat the seven clean pairs alongside the general two-of-every-kind command as a single refined instruction, not evidence of two fused accounts.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the flood account's precise, mathematical framework as the Priestly source's rewriting of the Jehovist's version, of which this animal count is one instance.

quotes.text: As to the contents of the story, the priestly version here agrees to an unusual extent with the Jehovistic one; differing from it chiefly in the artificial, mathematical marking out of the framework.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Priestly Code's mathematical reworking of the Jehovist flood narrative.

sides.snippet: you shall bring two of every sort into the ark, to keep them alive with you.
sides.verseText: Of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every sort into the ark, to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.

sides.snippet: You shall take seven pairs of every clean animal with you, the male and his female.
sides.verseText: You shall take seven pairs of every clean animal with you, the male and his female. Of the animals that are not clean, take two, the male and his female.
